notes: RW Aur A and B (1.5 arcsec apart) are one blended source: the photometry is A+B.
One frame per visit at 0.75 um, so no within-visit scatter. March 2026 has no frame near 0.75 um, so it has no point (its image is at another wavelength).

The calibration was checked against 2MASS/WISE on a field star (about 4%, D3), not on RW Aur, whose 2MASS epoch predates its dimming. A field star in the same frames holds at about 3.3 mJy, so the 2.5x brightening is the star, not the calibration.
Earlier sums of 65 to 90 mJy at 0.90 to 0.94 um were a masking artifact (the saturated peak was left out) and are not brightness.
Detected means S/N of at least 5 in a 2 px aperture on the stacked image (noise from blank spots in the same stack) and a centre within 1.5 px of the prediction.
No motion fit: 3 detected visits and 0.0 arcsec of expected drift; a fit needs 3 visits and half a pixel (3.1 arcsec).
Brightness: 3 px aperture, sky from 5 to 8 px, no aperture correction, frames within 0.009 um of 0.75 um only; saturated or masked frames are dropped, not guessed.

differences.note: A visual aid: the later visit minus the earlier, at the same wavelength. Static stars leave residuals of up to about 17% of their peak (the PSF is undersampled), so a change under about 10% of a star's peak cannot be flagged. Distances must come from the motion fit, not from these patches.
